payload.title: dispatch_change_intelligence decides what is already asked by re-planning the change's seats from today's workspace on every dispatch, so each fully seated merge ever recorded costs one closure computation per run (plus one service-facts computation per dispatch) and a later project rename or closure-order change re-asks an already reviewed change under a new seat name
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/pr_tracking.py:436-439 (the comment states the merge list only grows and per-merge cost must not scale per cycle)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/pr_tracking.py:459-467 (an already-seated change skips the mint-budget exit, so it proceeds to planning)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/pr_tracking.py:468-483 (service facts and _change_impact are computed from the live tree for every change with asked seats; missing is derived from today's plan)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/pr_tracking.py:304-321 (plan_change_seats names seats from the live closure order and project names)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/agent_invocations.py:2442-2445 (the ledger scan's own docstring says a per-subject cost must not grow with every merge ever recorded)
payload.rule_violated: SE-5 D-2 dedup contract: the ledger is the record of what was asked; a change asked about must not be asked again because the tree changed, and per-merge cost of the nightly dispatch must not grow with the merge history.
payload.notes: At the base an already-asked merge was a set lookup (pr_tracking.py at 91365f31a lines 330-334). Now every merge with a seated row runs cycle_service_examination, and the workspace's service facts are computed once per dispatch, on each nightly cycle, for as many merges as the ledger holds. Separately, after a change was asked with seats service:zz-core and lens, a commit that only renames the nx project owning libs/zz-core makes the next dispatch compute service:zz-core-renamed as missing and mint it for the same reviewed change (the same happens when closure order changes with more than three touched services). Both package reviewers reproduced the second effect with a rename probe; the architecture reviewer measured the first on this repository at about 1 s per change plus 14-19 s of service facts per dispatch. Close condition: Record the planned seat set (or a completion marker) on the change's first mint and read it back in dispatch, so a change whose recorded plan is fully asked is skipped from the ledger alone with no closure and no facts computation. Add tests: a rename after seating mints nothing, and a dispatch over N fully seated merges makes zero _change_impact calls. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
